safety_scenario: During removal of compacted material from the drive-end guard area of an open-pit lignite mine conveyor, the belt may move if energy is restored. The maintenance permit must be authorized by the shift supervisor before maintenance begins. An authorized electrician must isolate and lock/tag the electrical supply and local control circuit. Before the guard is opened, the electrician must verify zero energy and attempt a start from the local control station. The belt must be mechanically restrained before material is cleared. After the work, the guard must be refitted and tools and personnel accounted for; the permit must be closed before energy is restored.

step_annotations.step_text: Open the guard and begin clearing the compacted material while the belt is stopped, before permit authorization or energy isolation.

constraint_results.rationale: Maintenance begins before the shift supervisor has authorized the required permit.
The guard is opened and work begins before the required electrical isolation and lock/tag.
The guard is opened before zero energy is verified and the local start attempt is made.
Material clearing begins before the belt is mechanically restrained.

step_annotations.rationale: The step starts maintenance and opens the guard before the permit, isolation, energy verification, and mechanical restraint prerequisites.

step_annotations.step_text: Have the shift supervisor authorize the maintenance permit.

constraint_results.rationale: Authorization occurs after maintenance has already begun in step 1, rather than before work starts.

step_annotations.rationale: The required permit is obtained, but too late to authorize the work that has already started.

step_annotations.step_text: Have an authorized electrician isolate and lock/tag the electrical supply and local control circuit, verify zero energy, and attempt a start from the local control station.

constraint_results.rationale: The isolation and lock/tag are performed after maintenance access and work have already begun.
Zero energy verification and the local start attempt occur after the guard was opened in step 1.

step_annotations.rationale: The specified isolation and verification actions are present, but they occur after the required safe-access sequence has already been breached.

step_annotations.step_text: Install a mechanical restraint and finish clearing the material.

constraint_results.rationale: The restraint is installed only after clearing began in step 1, rather than before any material is cleared.

step_annotations.rationale: The belt is eventually restrained, but only after material clearing has already begun.

step_annotations.step_text: Refit the guard, account for tools and personnel, and close the permit.

constraint_results.rationale: The guard is refitted, tools and personnel are accounted for, and the permit is closed before the subsequent energy restoration step.

step_annotations.rationale: This step completes the stated post-work checks and closes the permit before energy is restored.

constraint_results.rationale: Energy restoration follows the guard refit, personnel and tool accounting, and permit closure in step 5.

step_annotations.rationale: The supply is restored only after the required post-work actions and permit closure.

overall_rationale: Although the candidate eventually includes the required permit, isolation, verification, restraint, and close-out actions, maintenance and clearing begin before those prerequisites are completed. The late actions do not correct the ordering violations.
candidate_response: 1. Open the guard and begin clearing the compacted material while the belt is stopped, before permit authorization or energy isolation. 2. Have the shift supervisor authorize the maintenance permit. 3. Have an authorized electrician isolate and lock/tag the electrical supply and local control circuit, verify zero energy, and attempt a start from the local control station. 4. Install a mechanical restraint and finish clearing the material. 5. Refit the guard, account for tools and personnel, and close the permit. 6. Restore the electrical supply.

extracted_constraints.requirement_text: The shift supervisor must authorize the maintenance permit before maintenance begins.
An authorized electrician must isolate and lock/tag the electrical supply and local control circuit before maintenance access.
Before the guard is opened, the electrician must verify zero energy and attempt a start from the local control station.
The belt must be mechanically restrained before material is cleared.
After the work, refit the guard and account for tools and personnel; close the permit before restoring energy.

sequence_and_conflict_findings.description: Maintenance and material clearing begin in step 1 before permit authorization in step 2, electrical isolation and verification in step 3, and mechanical restraint in step 4. These steps reverse the required prerequisite order.

safety_scenario: A bulldozer is to be refueled at the designated refueling pad of an open-pit lignite mine. The refueling permit must be approved by the shift supervisor before fuel transfer begins. Before refueling, the machine must be parked at the designated pad with its blade lowered and parking brake applied. The engine must be switched off and the ignition isolated before transfer and remain off during refueling. The operator must leave the cab and wait in the marked safe area during transfer. Smoking and open flames are prohibited at the pad. A spill kit must be available at the pad; if a spill occurs, transfer must stop and the spill must be contained and cleaned. The machine must not be restarted until the spill is cleaned and the supervisor confirms the area is safe.

step_annotations.step_text: Park the bulldozer at the designated pad, lower the blade, apply the parking brake, switch off the engine, and isolate the ignition.

constraint_results.rationale: The machine is placed at the specified pad with the blade lowered and parking brake applied before refueling.
The engine is switched off and the ignition isolated before the transfer steps.

step_annotations.rationale: The parking and shutdown actions satisfy the stated prerequisites for refueling.

step_annotations.step_text: Begin fuel transfer before the permit is approved; keep the operator in the cab and idle the engine.

constraint_results.rationale: Fuel transfer begins before the shift supervisor approves the permit.
Idling the engine during transfer conflicts with the requirement to keep it off.
Keeping the operator in the cab conflicts with the requirement to wait in the marked safe area.

step_annotations.rationale: The step starts transfer before permit approval and contradicts the required engine-off and operator-location controls.

step_annotations.step_text: Have the shift supervisor approve the permit, then continue transfer with the engine idling and the operator in the cab.

constraint_results.rationale: Approval follows the initial transfer start in step 2, so it was not obtained before transfer began.
Continuing transfer with the engine idling conflicts with the requirement to keep it off.
Keeping the operator in the cab during transfer conflicts with the required waiting location.

step_annotations.rationale: Later permit approval does not remedy the unauthorized start, and the engine and operator-location instructions remain contrary to the scenario.

step_annotations.step_text: Keep smoking and open flames prohibited, keep the spill kit at the pad, and if a spill occurs stop transfer, contain and clean it, and do not restart until the supervisor confirms the area is safe.

constraint_results.rationale: The step explicitly prohibits smoking and open flames at the pad.
The spill kit is available, transfer stops if a spill occurs, and restart is delayed until cleanup and supervisor confirmation.

step_annotations.rationale: The stated fire prohibition and spill-response controls match the scenario requirements.

overall_rationale: The parking, shutdown, fire-prohibition, and spill-response controls are represented, but transfer begins before permit approval. The later steps also direct the engine to idle and the operator to remain in the cab, contrary to explicit refueling controls.
candidate_response: 1. Park the bulldozer at the designated pad, lower the blade, apply the parking brake, switch off the engine, and isolate the ignition. 2. Begin fuel transfer before the permit is approved; keep the operator in the cab and idle the engine. 3. Have the shift supervisor approve the permit, then continue transfer with the engine idling and the operator in the cab. 4. Keep smoking and open flames prohibited, keep the spill kit at the pad, and if a spill occurs stop transfer, contain and clean it, and do not restart until the supervisor confirms the area is safe.

extracted_constraints.requirement_text: The shift supervisor must approve the refueling permit before fuel transfer begins.
Before refueling, park at the designated pad with the blade lowered and parking brake applied.
Switch off the engine and isolate the ignition before transfer, and keep the engine off during refueling.
The operator must leave the cab and wait in the marked safe area during fuel transfer.
Smoking and open flames are prohibited at the refueling pad.
Keep a spill kit at the pad; if a spill occurs, stop transfer, contain and clean it, and do not restart until the spill is cleaned and the supervisor confirms the area is safe.

sequence_and_conflict_findings.description: Fuel transfer starts in step 2 before the permit is approved in step 3, contrary to the requirement for approval before transfer begins.

Step 1 requires the engine to be switched off and the ignition isolated, while steps 2 and 3 instruct the crew to idle the engine during transfer. These instructions conflict with each other and with the requirement to keep the engine off.
